📺 LOOKING AT THE HIDDEN MARKET COLLAPSE + THE IMPORTANCE OF THE 8/21-DAY RULE + SEMIS / NEOCLOUD CAPITULATION + $TSLA LOOKS CONSTRUCTIVE

The biggest risk in this market isn't just how much individual stocks have already fallen. It's the massive divergence between what's happening beneath the surface and what the major indices are showing.

Some of the most popular growth, AI, and momentum stocks are already down 40%, 50%, even 80% from their highs:
– $IREN: -67%
– $NBIS: -45%
– $CRWV: -61%
– $AAOI: -70%
– $ASTS: -70%
– $OKLO: -82%
and the list goes on...

Yet, $SPY remains ONLY ABOUT 3% below its peak!

This is why the 8/21-day moving average rule is so important.

*
Many of these stocks were fantastic trades when they were trending above their 8-day and 21-day moving averages.

They generated enormous profits for disciplined momentum traders. But once they broke below those averages and failed to reclaim them, the character of those trades changed.

Don't turn great trades into terrible investments simply because you refuse to recognize a broken trend. Step aside, protect capital, and wait for the stocks to rebuild.

*

Today, watch $SPY $768 and especially $758.

Friday's low near $768 is the immediate reference point. A sustained break below $758 could signal a more significant correction, particularly as the weekly chart suggests the risk of a breakdown from its rising channel.

*

Meanwhile, the Mags are no longer providing the same support. $MAGS is showing a potential head-and-shoulders breakdown, while $AAPL suffered a failed breakout, and $META, $AMZN, and $GOOGL have weakened.

If the mega-cap stocks holding up the indices begin breaking down, something may finally give.

*

Important question this week: is capitulation approaching in semis and neoclouds:?

$MU, $SNDK, and even $INTC were tremendous momentum trades before the sector lost its 8/21-day structure around July 2. Since then, the selling has been relentless.

Neocloud stocks $NBIS $IREN have also been annihilated.

Following Elon Musk's weekend comments, I'm watching whether these names gap lower and reverse green, potentially signaling a washout, or continue selling as capitulation accelerates.

*

Amid all this weakness, $TSLA looks like one of the more constructive setups.

#Tesla is showing some commitment to its current trading area.

Earnings are behind us, and the stock is benefiting from an upgrade today. I'm not long yet because it hasn't provided a convincing entry.

But if #TSLA can consolidate, hold its gains, and eventually break above $388 and stay there, it could open the door to a test of more significant resistance.

I'll be watching Tesla closely today.

*

With the Fed on Wednesday and major Big Tech earnings ahead, this is not the time to deploy all your buying power or blindly short the indices.

Stay selective, respect your rules, and preserve capital.

Difficult markets eventually create better opportunities, but you need to protect yourself long enough to take advantage of them.

*

posts.name: Lance Breitstein 🇺🇸🌎
posts.text:
6 PLAYBOOKS FOR 6 DIFFERENT MARKET REGIMES

Last week’s firm-wide @smbcapital meeting was about better adapting to different market regimes.

Which begs the question - what types of market regimes are there for discretionary traders? And what playbooks should we be running for each of them?

I’ll start and you all can expand on this in the replies.

Obviously this is far from exhaustive and kept high-level, but I think this should lead serious traders to do some deep reflection of their own. 

1. Theme-driven bullish market. Markets like this one favor momentum strategies, swing longs, overnight momentum, IPOs, and headlines relevant to the driving theme.

Early summer of 2026 certainly fell under this with AI as the driver and leading sectors like DRAM / cloud computing.

2. Macro-driven markets. Think in the spring during the start of the U.S.-Iran conflict, think  2025 Trump tariffs and the Russia-Ukraine war. Due to the randomness and volatility of these headlines, this market highly favors breaking news trading as well as trading move-to-move, while greatly reducing overnight exposure and swing exposure. 

3. Range-bound market. Think of the last couple months, where we've had no prevailing theme and most indices have stayed range-bound while the leaders from the prior cycle corrected. In this market, you want to reduce overall trading activity and risk allocation. If volatility is inflated, you might focus on selling vol, but you need to be careful of complacency. There can still be niche opportunities, but overall, most traders will find it best to be more hands-off.

4. Panic-driven markets. During these markets, breakdowns can work exceptionally well. However, I found that my greatest PNL, ironically, comes from longs in names that have totally capitulated, especially trading the right side of the V. Overnights and swing trades can again be quite favorable in this market. IPOs and headlines tend to take a back seat.

5. Idiosyncratic single-stock or single-sector moves. This is the type of market where broader themes are quiet, yet single stock names occupy the majority of your focus. This is where all risk should be allocated to the single stock or sector. I'm thinking of when we saw the epic short squeeze in $CAR this year, or prior moves in names like $MSTR, $GME, $AMC, or when sectors offer great opportunities, like the quantum names over the last few years.

6. Euphoria. We've seen markets like this in 2021 following COVID, as well as glimpses of this at times during the last couple years. In this market, small caps are on fire. Anything with a theme works, and momentum breakouts go so much further than you could have imagined. This is when swing trading and big-picture imagination work better than you could have ever imagined. Those that are quick to short or skeptical either miss out or risk ruin, as using your brain can get you killed here. 

Further questions from here:
1. How do you identify each of these regimes FOR YOU? For example, one criteria might be a certain vix level or sentiment metric.
2. What playbooks are you competent in for each of those?
3. How much risk do each of these markets deserve?

This post was inspired by thoughts from @steenbab and this blog post:
http://traderfeed.blogspot.com/2026/10/best-practices-in-trading.html

Capital is now becoming the constraint…whoever can raise the most will win.

SpaceX has officially announced that they have secured $40 billion in the largest GPU financing ever.

The company entered into a $40B master finance lease for GPUs and related equipment with an entity managed by Apollo Global Management. This lease will deliver the next generation of NVIDIA Vera Rubin chips for SpaceX's terrestrial compute buildout and is an important step in our plan to build a Super Intelligence future. It represents the largest committed GPU financing ever.

SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen:
"SpaceX aims to deploy the largest compute infrastructure in the world. As demand for compute continues to accelerate, we're seeing less than one year payback periods on our SI infrastructure investments. This lease diversifies our funding sources and addresses a notable portion of the funding required to deliver on our growth plans as we aim to get additional compute online at record speeds to power Grok for enterprises and consumers, as well as serve existing and future cloud services customers."

Transaction Details:
The financing has been committed to by a number of financing parties led by Apollo and Goldman Sachs, who served as sole structuring agent. Entry into the lease remains subject to certain specified closing conditions and is expected to close prior to year-end 2026, with lease schedules expected to commence upon delivery of GPUs and related equipment in the first half of 2027.

posts.name: Rishi Mishra
posts.text:
Two reasons:

1. Elections that are this vital have usually been rare (getting more frequent now - think France, US, Canada last year, Brazil today). Most of the time elections don’t matter much for markets when there is some kind of centrist continuity to politics. 

2. When they do matter, upsets happen but typically from a 60-40, 66-33 setup instead of 80-20. 

Combined, this Brazil election becomes a huge surprise and hence feels extraordinary. But then again, it’s a binary, non-reflexive event (unlike the FOMC) so the odds don’t really have predictive power. It’s just a collective guess, and so expected to miss every now and then.

posts.name: Nick Timiraos
posts.text:
The Fed is expected to hold rates steady Wednesday, but it is a closer call on the data than the market-implied probabilities suggest.

The case for hiking: 
1) The hot September CPI and PPI underscore a second straight lost year for getting inflation down
2) With a Dec hike widely expected, hawks will argue that there's less to gain from waiting six weeks given the cost of falling further behind
3) Hawks will also argue that policy isn't restrictive and needs to be

The case for holding:
1) If officials still think this is a 2-3 hike recalibration, spacing out remaining moves costs little. "Being six weeks late is a manageable risk," says Rob Kaplan
2) Back-to-back moves could signal a faster cycle than officials intend
3) After several officials signaled no rush, and Warsh’s silence let odds of a hold build, a surprise hike days before the midterms would be a jolt. The Fed has raised rates right before elections, but not as a surprise

https://www.wsj.com/economy/central-banking/why-the-fed-is-expected-to-hold-rates-steady-despite-a-case-for-raising-them-3761e47f?st=GTvXjQ&reflink=desktopwebshare_permalink

posts.text: Republicans bragging about no tax on tips, overtime, or Social Security must also accept responsibility for higher inflation, as that was the trade-off. Because government spending actually rose as those tax cuts were enacted, the lost revenue means the tax cuts are paid for through higher inflation. So workers get to keep more of the money they earn, but its purchasing power is reduced by the higher prices that are a direct consequence of the tax cuts.
